units.title: A completed Ito process is integrable at a bounded stopping time
units.statement: Let eta be progressive and square-integrable on a positive finite horizon T, and let tau be a nonnegative stopping time with tau at most T pointwise. The completed Ito process I(eta) evaluated at tau is integrable.
assumptions: eta is a Samplinglib ProgressiveL2Integrand on a positive NNReal horizon T.
B is Brownian with respect to the filtration and measure; this contract implies that the measure is a probability measure.
The filtration satisfies Samplinglib's usual conditions.
tau is an NNReal-valued Chewi stopping time and tau(omega)≤T for every omega.
Lean requests an ambient finite-measure instance to elaborate the completed process; this is logically redundant because the Brownian contract supplies a probability measure.

steps.title: Stop the integrand
steps.text: Form the closed stopped integrand eta times the indicator of s≤tau. It remains progressive and L2 on the same horizon.

steps.title: Use terminal L2 integrability
steps.text: The terminal representative of the completed Ito integral of the stopped integrand belongs to L2, hence to L1 on the finite measure space.

steps.title: Identify random evaluation
steps.text: The completed bounded random-stopping theorem identifies that terminal representative almost everywhere with the original continuous Ito process evaluated at tau. Integrability transfers across almost-everywhere equality.

units.lean_statement: The theorem returns literal Bochner integrability of omega ↦ itoIntegralProcess eta ... (tau omega) omega under the ambient measure, with an explicit finite-measure typeclass already entailed by the Brownian contract.
units.lean_proof: The proof transfers the existing L1 property of the stopped terminal representative through the library's completed random-stopping almost-everywhere identity.
units.boundary: The theorem requires a positive finite construction horizon and a pointwise bounded NNReal stopping time. It does not cover unbounded stopping, local-L2 integrands before localization, vector stochastic integrals, or any Ito formula.

sources.label: Samplinglib completed bounded random-stopping identity
sources.scope: Almost-everywhere identification of the stopped terminal integral with random evaluation of the continuous completed Ito process.

units.title: A completed Ito process has mean zero at a bounded stopping time
units.statement: Under the same global L2, Brownian, usual-filtration, stopping-time, and pointwise horizon-bound assumptions, the integral of the completed Ito process evaluated at tau is zero.
assumptions: eta is a Samplinglib ProgressiveL2Integrand on a positive NNReal horizon T.
B is Brownian with respect to the filtration and measure, and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
tau is an NNReal-valued stopping time with tau(omega)≤T for every omega.
The theorem concerns the library's actual completed continuous Ito process, not an arbitrary process supplied together with a martingale premise.

steps.title: Use the stopped-integrand martingale
steps.text: The completed Ito process of the stopped integrand is a martingale and starts exactly at zero, including on the patched exceptional set.

steps.title: Compare deterministic times zero and T
steps.text: The martingale set-integral identity on the whole sample space makes the expectation at T equal the expectation at zero, hence zero.
steps.lean: Use Martingale.setIntegral_eq with the universal measurable set.

steps.title: Transfer to the bounded stopping time
steps.text: The terminal representative agrees almost everywhere both with J_T and with the original completed process I evaluated at tau. Integral congruence transfers the zero expectation.

units.lean_statement: The conclusion is the literal Bochner integral equality for random-time evaluation of the constructed completed Ito process.
units.lean_proof: The proof applies deterministic-time preservation of martingale expectation to the stopped integrand and then rewrites the terminal value using the two existing almost-everywhere consistency theorems.
units.boundary: This is not a general optional-sampling theorem and does not cover unbounded stopping times, local martingales without localization, vector stochastic integrals, quadratic variation, or Ito's formula.
